author: TEDx Talks
description:
We are reaching a point where distinguishing fact from fiction is becoming increasingly difficult. Dr. Myriam François argues that the rise of highly convincing AI-generated disinformation is unfolding alongside growing pressures on journalism and the institutions responsible for verifying and communicating facts.

As journalists face increasing threats and a small number of technology companies play a greater role in shaping how information is distributed, personalised algorithms can use our digital behaviour to influence what we see, believe, and engage with. This raises an important question: what happens when societies can no longer agree on a shared baseline of facts?

Without that common foundation, independent thought, public trust, and democratic participation can become increasingly fragile. Protecting the integrity of our information ecosystem is therefore not simply a challenge for journalists or technology companies, but a broader responsibility for all of us. Dr. François
title: How AI disinformation is reshaping our reality | Myriam Francois | TEDxCambridge University

author: TEDx Talks
description: What would banking look like with no interface at all, just a conversation in whatever language you already speak? This talk argues that our biggest risk isn't outdated technology; it's how comfortable we get with things that merely work. It challenges us to stop managing what's broken and start fixing it. Sulaiman Adewale is the founder of Xara, Africa's first AI-powered conversational banking assistant, built entirely inside WhatsApp. A self-taught software engineer from Osogbo, Osun State, he spent over a decade in software architecture before building Xara out of personal frustration: he found that even simple banking tasks meant fighting an interface that wasn't built for him. Rather than adapt to broken systems the way most of us quietly learn to, he asked what banking would look like with no interface at all, just a conversation, in whatever language a user already speaks, from Pidgin to Yoruba to Hausa. Launched in 2025, Xara now serves over sixty thousand users and has drawn
title: Adaptation: Our greatest undoing? | Sulaiman Adewale | TEDxOsogbo

author: TEDx Talks
description: How much of Africa actually exists in the datasets shaping today's AI? This talk makes the case that data is power, and that if Africa doesn't teach AI who it is, someone else will, with consequences for whether the continent is even part of the future conversation. Francis Odeyemi is a product and brand design leader and the founder of Ninthgrid, often called the "Shutterstock for Africa," a platform giving African photographers a way to earn from authentic, Afrocentric imagery while supplying brands with visual content that actually reflects the continent. Over more than a decade, he has built digital products across Nigeria, the UK, and the US, and is a Y Combinator Startup School alumnus with executive education from Stanford's Graduate School of Business. Through Ninthgrid, he has watched firsthand what happens when an AI model is asked to picture Africa, and how little of the continent actually exists in the datasets shaping today's AI. title: AI Is Learning. But About Africa? | Francis Odeyemi | TEDxOsogbo

author: TEDx Talks
description: "Follow your passion" is the most repeated advice young people receive. This talk challenges it, arguing that passion is fuel, not a destination: competence carries you, purpose gives you somewhere to go, and direction gets you there. It walks through the missing first step most people skip, and the real equation of value, scale, and trust behind sustainable success. Segun Solomon is the founder and CEO of Madros Technologies, where he leads IT consulting, digital skills development, and brand innovation across Nigeria. He also founded Tech Parrot, a technology media platform, and built the Madros Academy of Technologies into a training ground for thousands of young people entering the digital economy. Beyond his companies, Segun shapes policy as a member of the Technical Working Group under Nigeria's National Information Technology Development Agency and serves on the Osun State Advisory Board on Technology, Innovation, and Digital Economy. title: The World's Favorite Advice: "Follow Your Passion" | Segun Solomon | TEDxOsogbo

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk is about the moment of deciding to stop waiting (for permission, for the right conditions, for someone else to act) and start building the solutions you want to see. It's a decision that has already reshaped how thousands of women access care. Kemi Deborah Olakunle, known widely as Kemi the Changemaker, is a social entrepreneur with a background in Human Anatomy and advanced training in Public Health. She founded HealthVest, a health-tech venture whose flagship product, PreggiCare Wallet, helps women save toward pregnancy and childbirth while accessing discounted care. PreggiCare Wallet is one piece of her broader push for a Nigeria where quality healthcare isn't a privilege. She also leads the Art4Health Campaign and founded Changemakers Hub and Capital, which has trained and mentored over two thousand young people across multiple countries. Through the Solve Africa Fund, she's working to raise a million changemakers across Africa. This talk was given at a TEDx event using
title: The Day I Stopped Waiting | Kemi Deborah Olakunle | TEDxOsogbo

author: TEDx Talks
description: Public health isn't something that only happens in hospitals and ministries. This talk argues that it's built or broken in the everyday choices we make for ourselves and each other, and that everyone is already a public health actor, whether they have realized it or not. Oluwatomi Olunuga is a public health and development professional with over nine years of experience advancing health, gender equality, and the rights of women and girls across Nigeria and beyond. She is the founder of Careers in Public Health, which has supported over 3,400 students and professionals through mentorship and career development, and of the MaleMatters Initiative, which engages men and boys as partners in gender equity. Her work with organizations including UNFPA, Women Deliver, and GSMA, alongside her current role at Helium Health, has earned her recognitions including the Diana Award and a place on She Leads Africa's Top 50 Rising Moguls list. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conferenc
title: You are public health | Oluwatomi Olunuga | TEDxOsogbo

description: Can cruelty become so familiar that we stop recognizing it as cruelty? In this talk, the speaker shares the story of her family's adoption of a cat that had been a victim of abuse. This experience led her to reflect on how repeated exposure to cruelty can make us less sensitive to suffering and even cause us to accept it as normal. The talk invites us to question what we have become accustomed to, recognize the suffering of others, and remember that something does not become acceptable simply because we see it happen too often. description: Does struggling with math mean you are not intelligent? In this talk, the speaker reflects on a personal experience that sparked a deeper question about how we define intelligence and why academic grades often receive more recognition than creativity, artistic expression, and other talents. Drawing on Howard Gardner's theory of multiple intelligences, the talk challenges traditional ideas of academic success and explores how schools and society can better recognize different abilities. It invites us to rethink what it truly means to be intelligent and how education can prepare us for life beyond the classroom. Combining this personal experience with research on AI in education and examples of using AI as a creative partner, the talk explores the opportunities and risks of these tools. It challenges us to consider how AI can support, rather than replace, human imagination and creativity. Connecting this personal experience to psychological research on bias, the talk explores how our perceptions of others and ourselves can differ, reminding us that personal growth often happens quietly, one small change at a time. Drawing on the unlikely career wisdom of the cheetah, Fiona explores how understanding our needs can help us choose, adapt and build working environments in which people can thrive. Fiona is an accomplished senior executive, author and award winning advocate for diversity and inclusive leadership. She leverages her three decades of corporate experience with global brands across consumer goods and online marketplaces, along with her observations living in many countries and travelling widely, to bring fresh perspectives and help people to think differently about what is possible. description: Have you ever stayed quiet, avoided taking a risk, or changed your behavior because you were afraid of being judged? In this talk, the speaker explores the Spotlight Effect, a psychological phenomenon that makes us believe others pay more attention to us than they actually do. By examining how this illusion influences our choices, confidence, and self-expression, the talk invites us to question the limits we create out of fear of judgment and consider what we might do if we stopped worrying so much about how others see us. What if money could move as fast as information?

In this TEDx talk, Bala Nagaraj explores how tokenization is transforming the way we transfer and exchange value. Drawing on his experience in technology and banking, he explains why traditional financial systems struggle to keep up with the digital world and how turning money into programmable software could change that.

Beyond the technology, he raises a bigger question: If money becomes software, what kind of financial future do we want to build? Bala Nagaraj is a technology and innovation leader exploring how emerging technologies are transforming the future of finance. Drawing on experience across banking, product development, and digital innovation, he works at the intersection of AI, digital money, and blockchain, helping bridge the gap between technological possibility and real-world adoption. author: TEDx Talks
description:
At TEDxAvicenna Cinere School, themed “UNSEEN,” AVChestra presents two songs by the legendary band The Beatles: Yesterday and Let It Be.

Rather than simply reproducing the original arrangement, this performance reflects the spirit of exploration that AVChestra seeks to nurture. Through the process of studying, adapting and developing the arrangement, students experience how a familiar piece of music can be transformed into something new through their collective effort and musical understanding. Avicenna Orchestra, officially abbreviated as AVChestra is a student orchestra and a creative space for musical exploration and artistic development at SMP Avicenna Cinere. Established in 2024, AVChestra empowers students not only to perform music, but also to learn, experiment, collaborate, and take an active role in the creative process behind each musical performance. Through this experience, students are encouraged to be proactive, joyful and confident in exploring their musical potential.
title: Yesterday and Let It Be | Avicenna Orchestra | TEDxAvicenna Cinere School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
How often do our minds create entire realities out of nothing? This interactive presentation explores the phenomenon of "thoughts in transit"—the human tendency to dwell on what happened five minutes ago or worry about what will happen ten minutes from now, completely losing touch with the present moment.   

Through a guided audience experiment, the talk demonstrates how easily we surrender our personal power and awareness when we become consumed by our internal narratives. To regain control, the core message emphasizes the importance of grounding ourselves in our five physical senses—sight, smell, taste, touch, and hearing. Ultimately, the presentation challenges the audience with a profound choice: to remain trapped in fleeting thoughts, or to harness sensory awareness and become an active observer of life.  Dr. Sheetal Soni is a Spirituality Observer and comes with over 20+ years of experience as a Motivational Speaker and a Life Coach. She is distinct with few accolades unique to
title: Escaping the Illusions of the Mind | Dr. Sheetal Soni | TEDxCUH

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What defines a true leader when formal titles and corporate certifications are stripped away? This talk challenges the modern notion that leadership requires a specific designation by examining the profound legacies of history’s most influential figures.   

By exploring the philosophical credibility of Socrates, the shared hardships of Alexander the Great, and the merit-based ecosystems of Genghis Khan, the presentation highlights how monumental impact is built on conviction and shared struggle. It further illustrates that leadership transcends age, gender, and authority through the boundless curiosity of Leonardo Da Vinci and the fearless devotion of figures like Joan of Arc and Birsa Munda.   

Ultimately, the core message serves as a timeless call to action: leadership is an ethical responsibility driven by courage and morality, not a title waiting to be handed out.  Swati Kumari is an educator, career counsellor, corporate trainer, and communication coach with over 12 years of ex
title: You Don't Need a Title to Lead | Swati Kumari | TEDxCUH

This talk explores the evolution of financial freedom, from early human cooperation to modern approaches centered on individual financial independence. Drawing on historical developments, demographic changes, and personal experiences during Lebanon's economic crisis, it examines the role of community, knowledge sharing and collaboration in achieving long term financial security. Charbel's approach is grounded in behavioral coaching, the belief that financial outcomes
are shaped as much by psychology and decision patterns as by market fundamentals. The belief that financial planning should exist to support the ultimate version of a life of happiness, which undermines greed-investing, and focuses on the enabling of a peaceful existence. His 29 years operating in Lebanon and the region give him rare first-hand exposure to a wide array of decision-making patterns, and success practices, whether in life or in investing.
After 17 years of Atlantis Group, and multiple achievements in their f
title: Jurassic finance | Charbel Khoury | TEDxNDULouaize

author: TEDx Talks
description:
At ten, while other children worried about homework, Ethish Gowda couldn’t stop asking why we are alive. That question took a boy from Hariyabbe, a village in Chitradurga district, through Sanskrit and the Vedas to entrepreneurship. It led him to move to Bengaluru at 15 and to plan his life decades ahead. Now 18, he shares the shift that changed everything: from asking “What do I want?” to asking “Who do I need to become to make it happen?” Ethish Gowda is an 18-year-old digital marketer, creative thinker and entrepreneur from Hariyabbe, a small village in Karnataka's Chitradurga district. Raised in a humble household, he has been driven from an early age by curiosity, creativity and a determination to turn bold ideas into reality.
Despite his age, Ethish has built hands-on experience across digital marketing, social media, branding and creative communication, and continues to explore new ways to use these skills to create meaningful impact. His journey from a rural village to the wor
title: Become the Person Your Dream Needs | Ethish Gowda | TEDxDavangere

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In 1958, a young engineer from Rameswaram finished ninth in a selection for eight Air Force pilot positions. He never became a pilot. Instead, he built India’s rockets and became its President. Through Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam’s story and her own journey from Uttar Pradesh to IIT Bombay, Ojasvi Verma argues that opportunity in India is not unevenly available but unevenly known. She gives students a three-step map to close that gap: Explore, Decide, Squeeze Ojasvi Verma is an IIT Bombay alumna, a Senior Manager at Intuit, and the creator of the YouTube channel Ojasvi Verma [IIT Bombay], where more than 40,000 students turn to her guidance on exams, internships, scholarships and careers.
Her own path was far from clear at the start. She went on to clear GATE along with the ISRO and BARC scientist recruitment examinations, and has worked with the Tata Group and NITI Aayog. She later became the youngest manager on her team, working directly with CEOs.
A returning TEDx speaker, Ojasvi has ju
title: The Career Map Nobody Gives You | Ojasvi Verma | TEDxDavangere

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When a child loses a chess match, we say failure is the best teacher. When the same child fails a science exam, the lecture begins. Educationist and author Saina Ubhrani examines this double standard. She asks whether our obsession with marks, medals and right answers is quietly teaching children to stop questioning. She makes a compelling case for raising achievers who can think, and for making life skills like empathy, financial literacy and respectful disagreement part of growing up. Saina Ubhrani is an educationist, entrepreneur, author and speaker with nearly two decades of experience in education. She holds an MBA in Marketing and Finance and began her career in Pune, working across sales, education and image consulting before turning her focus to early childhood learning.
She is co-founder and director of Chocolate Kids Preschool in Bilaspur, where she has worked closely with young children and their parents since 2013, gaining a first-hand view of how children learn, grow and
title: Are We Raising Achievers or Thinkers? | Saina Ubhrani | TEDxDavangere

description:
Not every crisis has a hidden purpose, and you don’t have to be grateful for your pain. Drawing on a period when his own plans and confidence fell apart, AI engineering leader Naveen K. Reddy offers an honest alternative to toxic positivity. His C.A.S.H. framework has four steps: Cut the expectations, Audit the pain, Spend the energy, Hold the character. It is a compassionate guide to turning hardship into character, one honest step at a time. Naveen K. Reddy is Senior Manager of AI Engineering at Ecolab, where he turns ambitious enterprise AI initiatives into measurable, production-grade results, working at the intersection of deep technical engineering and commercial strategy, with a focus on autonomous systems and responsible AI.

Before Ecolab, Naveen held technology leadership roles at Aptiv, EY and Deloitte, building and scaling AI products across sustainability, automotive, telecom and retail. He champions a "Production on Day One" approach to engineering and has helped transfo
title: Crisis as Capital: Turning Hardship Into Character | Naveen K Reddy | TEDxDavangere

author: TEDx Talks
description:
India tops the world in plastic pollution, yet Indians use far less plastic per person than Europeans or Americans. So what is going wrong? Engineer and entrepreneur Arijit Das argues that India doesn’t have a consumption problem; it has a collection problem. He maps the four places where the waste chain breaks and shows the machines his team built to fix three of them. He also makes a bold case that cleaning up India is not just a cause to support but a field to build a career in. Arijit Das is a computer science engineer and co-founder of Aeonix Research and Innovations, a bootstrapped Indian deep-tech company that builds complete technology systems for defence, government and enterprise, designing everything in-house, from circuit boards and firmware to AI and cloud software.
He started the company with no capital, no clients and no manufacturing facility. Today its systems are used by the Indian Army and large multinational companies, and run in more than ten countries. He is also
title: India’s Plastic Problem Isn’t What You Think | Arijit Das | TEDxDavangere

description:
Your first interview, your first presentation, your first time travelling alone: every “first” comes with racing thoughts and sweaty palms. Drawing on a nerve-wracking solo journey to Germany, dentist-turned-trainer Dr. Sandhya Arunkumar reframes discomfort as the growth zone. She shares SAIL (Sigh, Absorb, Interrogate and Link), a simple four-step method to calm your body, steady your mind and build lasting self-trust. It is a practical toolkit for anyone about to step into the unknown. Dr. Sandhya Arunkumar is a keynote speaker and trainer in personal growth and communication. A dentist by training, she has spent more than 20 years as a professor of dentistry, bringing the discipline of a clinician and the patience of a teacher to everything she does.
A journey of self-discovery in her late thirties changed the direction of her work. Since then, she has led more than 500 sessions reaching over 10,000 people, from students to senior leaders, on positive communication, public speaking
title: Why Your Brain Needs Evidence, Not Courage | Dr. Sandhya Arunkumar | TEDxDavangere

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when career plans collide with life's unexpected detours?   

This talk explores the unpredictable nature of professional trajectories, tracing a drastic pivot from stem cell research and a PhD in blood cancer to surprising, confidence-building ventures into theater and stand-up comedy. It highlights how years of rigorous scientific work in CRISPR and immunotherapy can unexpectedly reveal a completely different calling during a global crisis.   

Addressing a critical gap in patient care—where medical professionals often lack the time to answer fundamental emotional and psychological questions—the presentation delves into the profound shift from clinical oncology to mental health counseling. By introducing the "CHAI" framework (Challenge: Accept, Adapt, Evolve, Enjoy), the core message advocates for nurturing the inner child, remaining adaptable, and embracing the uncertainty of whatever card life reveals next. Dr. Amit Sharma is a Counselling Psychologist and Psycho-Onco
title: The "CHAI" Framework for Life's Unexpected Challenges | Dr. Amit Sharma | TEDxCUH

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the most valuable lessons in your career didn't come from reaching your destination, but from the detours along the way?   

Drawing on a non-linear transition from molecular biology to an MBA and product management, this speaker explores how professional trajectories rarely follow a straight line. Through five core lessons, the talk presents an approach to navigating career transitions, emphasizing that our best ideas and true growth happen "in transit." 

The central idea is simple: every unrelated experience, difficult job, or unexpected change in direction compounds over time to build your unique capabilities. By remaining curious and learning from the problems we face, we can transform uncertainty into a career superpower.   Mayank Bansal is a Product Innovation and Growth Leader with nearly 16 years of experience transforming ideas into commercially successful products, building high-performing teams, and enabling organizations to grow through innovation, strategy, and c
title: The Career You Planned vs The Person You Become | Mayank Bansal | TEDxCUH

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the most essential ingredient in any successful exchange is the one thing technology cannot transmit?   

In an era where information travels globally in minutes, this talk explores the irreplaceable value of the "human touch"—the tacit knowledge and emotional connection that cannot be digitized or automated. Through relatable examples, such as sharing an exact recipe across the world only to find the recreated dish missing a vital, unspoken essence, the speaker illustrates that precise data and measurements are never enough on their own.  
 
Whether it is the comforting taste of a meal cooked by a mother, the spontaneous bonding of stranded passengers after a delayed flight, or the communal experience of breaking bread together, human interaction remains at the core of our most meaningful experiences. As automation and robotics increasingly handle everyday tasks like cooking and serving, the speaker argues that the simple act of gathering people together will remain our great
title: The Uncopyable Ingredient: Why the Human Touch Defies Technology | Sameer Lamba | TEDxCUH
